oracle.definition: candidate and incumbent scored with the exact verifier on the same fresh T_RULE items (purpose 'oracle', index = decision index, tracker pool minus start-map and tracker uids); improved iff mean over T_RULE slices of (candidate - incumbent) > improvement_threshold; accepted iff the first verdict classifies as 'accept' (gated and ungated arms alike); false-accept rate = accepted and not improved / not-improved blocks; false-reject rate = not accepted and improved / improved blocks

counting.operator_calls: as reported by the operators: GRPO 2 forward calls (generate + training forward) and 1 backward per update; ES 1 generation call per member (plus extra batches)
counting.fpe: sequence level: every generated sequence and every training-forward sequence = 1 forward, every backward sequence = 2 forwards

definitions.pairing: Every statistic is a paired difference over seeds: arms with the same seed share the start checkpoint, the sampler root seed and hence every tracker / oracle item. Scope: every seed of a run also shares one split, one start checkpoint (after SFT), one start map and one informed channel selection (made once on the start model); the arm seed varies only the RL stage (the sampler root, i.e. every item drawn through the arm's sampler: gate, tracker, oracle and training (GRPO prompt / ES fitness) items, the operator seed and the es_random draw). The intervals therefore cover RL-stage randomness only, conditional on this split, start and selection, not SFT or selection variance. Interval: two-sided 1 - criteria_alpha Student-t over seeds (paired_interval). Fewer than 3 paired seeds or a missing counterpart arm -> INCONCLUSIVE, never SUCCESS or KILL.
definitions.gate: Per operator and seed: leak variant d_hack = hack_rate_final(gate_off) - hack_rate_final(gate_on) and d_T = T_rule_final(gate_on) - T_rule_final(gate_off); clean variant c = T_rule_final(gate_on) - T_rule_final(gate_off); each averaged over the operators that have all four arms for that seed. SUCCESS: interval(d_hack).lo > 0 and interval(d_T).lo > 0 and mean(c) >= -se(c) (clean T_rule within one standard error of gate-off). KILL: the clean-run T_rule cost exceeds the planted-run gain, tested paired: k = -c - d_T per seed, interval(k).lo > 0; or the first verdicts (all arms, both gate settings) reject more than half of the blocks the oracle marks as improved (evaluable only with >= min_improved_blocks such blocks). SUCCESS requires both KILL conditions to be evaluable: with fewer than min_improved_blocks oracle-improved blocks the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE ('reject-rate KILL not evaluable'), whatever the intervals show (the k KILL still applies). Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. T_rule_final = tracker T_rule of the weights after the last update, measured at the tracker step oracle_exclusion_steps(config), the same for every arm (so same-seed arms' finals are scored on identical tracker items whatever their decision counts); hack_rate_final = V1-pass & V2-fail share of the last block_updates updates' training rollouts. Every gate verdict carries gate_exercise: when fewer than min_improved_blocks blocks are oracle-improved or the gate accepted no block, the reason says 'gate not exercised' and the error rates are reported as not evaluable / not informative.
definitions.subset: Per seed (averaged over the gate settings and variants present for both arms): d_R = R_mean(es_informed) - R_mean(es_random), d_T = T_rule(es_informed) - T_rule(es_random), d_A = A(es_informed) - A(es_random) at the end of training. 'Equal A': |mean(d_A)| <= equal_a_tolerance. SUCCESS: equal A and (interval(d_R).lo > 0 or interval(d_T).lo > 0). KILL: equal A and neither interval excludes zero in favour of the informed subset (no separation). INCONCLUSIVE: A not equal, or < 3 seeds. The informed subset is one fixed selection shared by every seed (only the density-matched random control is redrawn per seed), so a verdict is about this selection, not about the selection procedure. Reported beside it: each subset's A gain since its step-0 tracker point (a no-separation KILL where neither subset acquired anything is vacuous and should be read as such).
definitions.operator: Per seed, GRPO arm (clean variant and gate_off if present, else the first available): G = T_rule_final - T_rule at the arm's own step-0 tracker point (not the start map: one fixed sample shared by every seed would add a bias the interval cannot see) and budget B = operator_budget_factor x its total forward-pass equivalents (sequence level: each generated or training-forward sequence = 1, each backward sequence = 2). ES arm (operator_es_arm, same variant and gate): T_rule gain (relative to its own step-0 point) at its last tracker point with cumulative FPE <= B (one point, like GRPO's final point; not a maximum over noisy points, which would favour ES by selection); r = gain - operator_gain_fraction x G. SUCCESS: interval(r).lo > 0 and mean(G) > 0. KILL: interval(r).hi < 0, mean(G) > 0 and the ES arm spent at least B in every seed. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (in particular when GRPO gained nothing or ES stopped before spending B). kill_reachable (statistic) = the ES arm spent B in every paired seed (None without a paired seed); when it is False every reason says 'Operator KILL not reachable' and the run warns: only SUCCESS or INCONCLUSIVE were possible (raise es_updates).
definitions.low_start: Start pass@k (k = start_k, sampled) on t_rule/unseen_pairs versus each arm's final greedy pass@1 on that slice (tracker), per seed. SUCCESS: some arm (operator x gate x variant) has interval(final - start_pass_k).lo > 0. KILL: every arm has interval.hi <= 0 (none exceeds the start's pass@k: the task is acquisition-limited; reported, the task is not weakened). Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. The start pass@k is one sample shared by every arm and seed, so its sampling error is common to all paired differences: each interval adds se_start = baseline_standard_error(pass_k, start items) (binomial bound, never 0); the interval half-width is the quadrature sum of the seeds' t half-width and the baseline's half-width (interval_with_baseline_error). Several arms are compared without a multiplicity correction (stated, not corrected).
